summary:
## Project Overview A Godot 4.5 2D character-movement prototype built with standard scene composition. The project uses a hierarchical scene chain (`Main → Game → Player`) with the Player as an instanced `PackedScene`, and no autoloads. The main entry point is `res://scenes/main.tscn` configured in `res://project.godot`. ## System Modules | Module | Responsibility | Key Files | Key Functions/Signals | |--------|---------------|-----------|----------------------| | **Player Controller** | Handles 2D character physics and input-driven movement (up/down/left/right). | `res://scripts/player.gd`
`res://scenes/player.tscn` | `CharacterBody2D` derived script; 3 methods (e.g. `_ready`, `_physics_process`, `_input` or equivalent); consumes actions `move_left`, `move_right`, `move_up`, `move_down`. | | **Game Level** | Gameplay container/world that owns the Player instance. | `res://scenes/game.tscn` | Root `Node2D` that instances `res://scenes/player.tscn` via `[ext_resource]`. | | **Main Bootstrap** | Top-level scene launched by the project; loads the Game scene. | `res://scenes/main.tscn`
`res://project.godot` | Root `Node` → child `Game` (`Node2D`); set as `main_scene` in `project.godot`. | ## Dependencies & Signal Flow - `Main` depends on `Game`: `res://scenes/main.tscn` contains a `Game` child node (`Node2D`) that is the active game world. - `Game` depends on `Player`: `res://scenes/game.tscn` instances the external `PackedScene` `res://scenes/player.tscn`. - `Player` depends on project input map: `move_left`, `move_right`, `move_up`, `move_down` are defined in `res://project.godot`. - No autoloads are registered. - No custom signals or cross-node signal chains have been observed. ## Issues Found - **Scene rebuild failures:** `build_scene` was called twice on existing scenes (`res://scenes/game.tscn` and `res://scenes/main.tscn`), requiring a fallback to `patch_scene`. - **Player node type regression in `game.tscn`:** After a `patch_scene` removal/replacement, `game.tscn` temporarily contained a bare `Node` named `Player` instead of instancing the `CharacterBody2D` Player scene, breaking the intended composition. - **Manual text replacement risk:** `replace_in_file` was used to edit `.tscn` files directly, which can produce invalid scene data if not perfectly aligned with Godot’s expected `[ext_resource]`/`[node]` structure. - **Script re-attachment churn:** The Player script had to be re-attached via `patch_scene` after scene edits, indicating scene references were lost during modification. - **Inconsistent intermediate state:** Round 16 removed the Player from `game.tscn`, yet a subsequent `read_file_tail` still showed the Player node present, suggesting read-after-write or caching inconsistency during the edit sequence. - **No signals / autoloads yet wired:** The project currently lacks event-driven architecture, state managers, or UI systems.
